TWF.label: Tool Wear Failure
TWF.summary: Cutting tool has reached the end of its usable life; edges worn, about to break in the cut. Failure point is random in the 200-240 min window, so this is a risk window, not a certainty.
recommended_actions: Schedule a tool change at the next planned stop
Inspect cutting edge and finish on recent parts
Reset the tool-wear counter after replacement
TWF.consequence: Tool breaks mid-cut, scrapping the workpiece and possibly marking the spindle — a routine swap becomes an unplanned overstrain-class event.

HDF.label: Heat Dissipation Failure
HDF.summary: Process is not shedding heat fast enough (temp difference < 8.6 K while spindle < 1380 rpm). Friction heat accumulates; thermal drift pushes parts out of tolerance.
recommended_actions: Clear blocked coolant lines or clogged filters
Verify chiller / heat exchanger is running
Reduce spindle load or raise speed if coolant is nominal
parts_required: Heat exchanger service kit (if chiller implicated)
HDF.consequence: Out-of-tolerance parts pass inspection and reach the customer; sustained overheating shortens spindle-bearing life.

PWF.label: Power Failure
PWF.summary: Mechanical power (torque x angular velocity) has left the 3,500-9,000 W safe band. Under-power = tool stalling; over-power = drive being overdriven. Opposite fixes.
recommended_actions: If under-power/stall: raise spindle speed or reduce feed; check for a binding or dull tool
If over-power/overdrive: reduce feed rate; inspect spindle drive, motor current, belt tension; check for a seized axis
parts_required: Usually none for a parameter fix
Spindle drive / motor inspection kit if over-power persists
PWF.consequence: Spindle-motor or drive burnout — a multi-hour, multi-thousand-dollar replacement instead of a parameter change.

OSF.label: Overstrain Failure
OSF.summary: Tool wear x torque has exceeded the overstrain limit for the variant (11,000/12,000/13,000 minNm for L/M/H). A worn tool pushed at high torque; combined strain can snap the tool and damage workpiece or spindle. Most severe mode.
recommended_actions: Stop the operation before the next cut
Reduce feed rate by ~15% to bring wear x torque under the limit
Inspect workpiece and spindle for damage before resuming
OSF.consequence: Catastrophic tool fracture: scrapped part, possible spindle damage, and the longest unplanned downtime of any mode.

RNF.label: Random Failure
RNF.summary: Random failure with no sensor signature; 0.1% chance regardless of parameters, irreducible. Cannot be diagnosed or predicted.
RNF.consequence: None predictable. Belongs on the limitations slide.
